description: Four drum voices playing from ten style presets, each voice holding two alternative sounds that a chance control picks between, with a stereo mix and an output per voice

params.text: Chooses one of ten presets, each setting the mode, pitch, decay, sweep and bend of all eight sounds: West African, Afro-Cuban, Brazilian, Balkan, Indian, Gamelan, Jazz, Electronic, Breakbeat, Techno
Sets how far apart the four voices are placed in the stereo mix, all in the centre at 0% and at their full spread at 100%
Sets the chance that a trigger fires that voice's second sound rather than its first, 0% for always the first and 100% for always the second
Shifts the pitch of both of that voice's sounds, one octave down fully anticlockwise to one octave up fully clockwise
Multiplies the decay of both of that voice's sounds, a fifth of the preset length at the bottom of its travel to twice it at the top

inputs.text: Added to the STYLE knob, one preset per volt; the total is held between the first and the tenth
A rising edge through 2V fires that voice, with the VOICE knob deciding which of its two sounds is used
Read at the moment of a trigger and sets the level of that hit, silent at 0V and full at 10V; unpatched, every hit is at full level
Added to that voice's FREQ knob, a fifth of an octave per volt; the total is held within one octave either way
Added to that voice's DECAY knob, 0.18 of the multiplier per volt; the total is held between a fifth of the preset length and twice it

outputs.text: That voice's two sounds added together, ±5V, before the panning
The left side of the four voices panned by SPREAD and soft-clipped to ±5V
The right side of the four voices panned by SPREAD and soft-clipped to ±5V

notes: no sound is made until a rising edge reaches a trigger jack. A voice whose trigger jack is empty is not even scanned.
the four rows are the roles Lead, Groove, Timeline and Foundation from the top down, and the name beside each row is drawn at runtime rather than printed on the panel.
both of a voice's sounds are always sounding out; a trigger restarts one of them while the other carries on decaying, so the voice output can carry two overlapping hits.
